newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO chief urges Turkey not to block expansion.
newsitem.headline: NATO chief urges Turkey not to block expansion.

text.p: NATO Secretary General Javier Solana urged Turkey on Monday not to block enlargement of the western military alliance in a bid to pressure the European Union to take it in as a member.

Referring to threats by Ankara to block the NATO expansion unless the 15-nation EU includes it in its own separate eastern expansion, Solana told the European Parliament's foreign affairs committee he hoped this was just politicking.

"The last time I spoke to the Turkish leaders they stressed a link between ratification of the enlargement of NATO and the enlargement of the EU," Solana told the deputies during a question and answer session.
"I would like to think that these are more political statements than statements which take effect. I do not want NATO enlargement to be conditional on what happens in any other forum."
NATO intends to invite a number of former foes from behind the Iron Curtain to membership talks at its Madrid summit on July 8-9.

The United States, NATO's most powerful member, set the agenda last week when it said NATO's first expansion to the former communist bloc should be limited to three countries -- Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary -- and said it expected its wish to prevail.

The leaders of France and Germany defied Washington on Friday by insisting they would support bids by Romania and Slovenia to join the alliance and the two countries concerned vowed to try to get Washington to change its mind.
But even if the NATO members reach a consensus ahead of the Madrid summit -- as Solana told deputies he hoped they would do over the next "days or weeks" -- Turkey's threat remains.

Turkey, a NATO member since 1952, strategically placed at the doorway to Asia, is a close ally of Washington and observers question whether it would risk irking the United States by going all the way and blocking the project.

But, resentful of the European Union's refusal on human rights grounds to embrace Turkey, Ankara has maintained its question mark over the NATO expansion in a bid to exercise leverage over the European countries which belong to both groups.
